text: Bees cull their several sweets from this flower and that blossom, here and there where they find them, but themselves afterwards make the honey, which is all and purely their own, and no more thyme and marjoram: so the several fragments he borrows from others, he will transform and shuffle together to compile a work that shall be absolutely his own; that is to say, his judgment.
author: Michel de Montaigne
locator: Book I, Chapter 25, Of the Education of Children
translation: Charles Cotton, ed. W. C. Hazlitt, 1877
